rows.claim: 1 Acceptance: author gate accepts R/bundle_r2 with AUTHOR_CONTRACT_CONSISTENT (2 requirements, 2 cases)
rows.note: Reproduced verbatim against the published bundle; requirements=2 and cases=2 match 05_M1_M4_results.json. Negative ceiling fields (checker NOT_RUN, release FAIL_CLOSED) are present, so the pass cannot be read as a native claim.

rows.claim: 1a Refusal: gate refuses a copy of bundle_r2 with PlannedTQAEP.json deleted
rows.command: PY scripts/pre_v2_gate_r2.py p0/tamper/c1_missing_tqaep   (copy of bundle_r2 with PlannedTQAEP.json removed)
rows.observed: {"verdict":"FAIL_CLOSED","first_fail":"[WinError 2] the system cannot find the file specified: 'C:\\...\\p0\\tamper\\c1_missing_tqaep\\PlannedTQAEP.json'"}
rows.note: Refuses and exits non-zero, so the claim holds. Weakness worth recording before publication: the refusal surfaces as an untyped OSError string that echoes an absolute host path, not as a typed code such as ARTIFACT_MISSING:PlannedTQAEP.json. 05_M1_M4_results.json's wording 'file missing (fail closed)' is accurate but the raw first_fail is not machine-classifiable.

rows.claim: 1b Refusal: gate refuses a copy whose PI polarity is flipped and its digest re-signed
rows.command: PY resign.py p0/tamper/c1_polarity polarity  (PI.requirements[0].polarity POS->NEG, then re-signed PD.pi_digest, ECP.pd_digest, manifest artifact shas and candidate_sha256) && PY scripts/pre_v2_gate_r2.py p0/tamper/c1_polarity
rows.note: The whole re-sign chain had to be forged (PI sha, PD.pi_digest, ECP.pd_digest, candidate digest, manifest) for the gate to reach the semantic layer, and it still refused. Confirms the reported first_fail exactly: the digest seal alone cannot launder a polarity flip; the registry is the real anchor.

rows.claim: 1c Refusal: gate refuses a copy with an injected checker receipt key
rows.command: PY resign.py p0/tamper/c1_receipt receipt  (adds top-level 'checker_execution_receipt' to PlannedTQAEP.json, re-signed) && PY scripts/pre_v2_gate_r2.py p0/tamper/c1_receipt
rows.note: Exact match to the reported first_fail. Note the injection does not move candidate_sha256 (PlannedTQAEP is outside the three-body candidate frame), so only the FORBIDDEN key walk catches it - and it does, because walk_no_credentials runs before the per-body schema check.

rows.claim: 2 Acceptance: pipd validate --bundle R/c2/bundle.json --require-four => FOUR_OBJECT / complete true / checked 4
rows.observed: checked=4, closure=FULL, complete=true, missing=[], required=[PI-PKG,PD-PKG,ECP,TQAEP], scope=FOUR_OBJECT, verdict=PASS, findings=[]

rows.claim: 2b Refusal: same command on R/01_products/pipd/bundle_missing_tqaep.json => PARTIAL_BUNDLE and fails closed with exit != 0
rows.observed: checked=3, complete=false, scope=PARTIAL_BUNDLE, verdict=FAIL, missing=[TQAEP], findings=[{contract:'*',kind:'DENOMINATOR',detail:'missing required object(s): TQAEP'}]
rows.note: Exact match to R/01_products/pipd/m2b_strict.out. Precision for the published text: the same bundle WITHOUT --require-four exits 0 / verdict PASS / scope PARTIAL_BUNDLE (reproduced, matches m2b_partial.out). Fail-closed comes from the flag, not from the validator default - do not state it as 'a missing TQAEP fails validation'.

rows.command: PYTHONPATH=patch/pipd-wt/src .venv-pipd/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_pre_v2_adapters.py -k 'fake_grant_refused or cross_subject_refused or blind_retry_refused' -v

rows.claim: 5 Extra falsification: bundle_r2 with PI.json replaced by the real canonical R/01_products/pipd/pi.json, no re-signing
rows.note: The gate fails, but one layer earlier than a reader might expect: the manifest artifact sha is checked before anything semantic, so a genuine-but-unbound canonical PI is rejected as a hash mismatch and never reaches PI_TRACE_OR_ORACLE_MISMATCH or PI_BINDING. Correct fail-closed behaviour, and evidence that a swapped-in 'real' artifact cannot be smuggled past the manifest.

rows.claim: 6 Extra falsification: no code path mints grant / nonce / QUALIFIED / INDEPENDENT_PASS / signed_verdict
rows.command: grep -rn -i over patch/sbl-tpm-sp for each token, code scope (py/json/yaml) excluding references/corpus; plus mint/issue/emit/sign scan of scripts/ and skills/, plus manual read of core.py:306-311, check_semantics.py:29-34, pre_v2.py:13-14,36,41
rows.observed: In code the five tokens appear only as: FORBIDDEN/ESCALATIONS/BAD_CLAIMS denylists (pre_v2.py:13-14, pre_v2_gate_r2.py:19-25), refusal branches (need(...)/raise Refusal('EXTERNAL_RAW_AND_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED') in core.py:307, FORBIDDEN_AUTHORITY_KEY/FORBIDDEN_DESIGN_CLAIM in pre_v2.py:36,41, claim_gate error in check_semantics.py:32), schema consts that pin the opposite state ('independent_acceptance': 'NOT_GRANTED', 'grant_state': 'NOT_GRANTED'), negative-test strings and descriptive text. No mint/issue/emit/sign helper exists in scripts/ or skills/.
rows.note: One honesty caveat rather than a refutation: the phrase 'appear only as denylist/forbidden keys' is slightly too strong. skills/pipd-package-project/{input,output}.schema.json list LOCAL_QUALIFIED and INDEPENDENT_PASS as admissible allowed_claims VALUES, and the claim_gate rule will pass such a case only when an externally supplied approval_receipt AND checker_identity are present. So the plugin can propagate a ceiling someone else established; it cannot create the evidence. Say 'no code path mints' - do not say 'the strings never appear as accepted values'.
